hook: Engineers at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology just created a new device that calculates using mechanical movements.

sections.voiceover: Engineers at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology just created a new device that calculates using mechanical movements.
sections.visual_cue: Close-up of a soft polymer film under a scanning electron microscope.

sections.voiceover: Researchers at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology developed tiny soft polymer nanodevices. How do these mechanical movements emulate neuronal behavior?
sections.visual_cue: Microscopic view of soft polymer structures shifting shape.

sections.voiceover: Except these nanodevices achieve this functionality using energy-efficient mechanical motion instead of traditional electricity.
sections.visual_cue: Comparison graphic showing electrical circuit versus mechanical movement.

sections.voiceover: Farnaz Niroui and her team published these findings in the journal Science Advances. These devices mimic neuronal behavior through viscoelastic nanomechanical properties.
sections.visual_cue: Portrait shot of Farnaz Niroui overlaid with the Science Advances journal cover.

sections.voiceover: The U.S. National Science Foundation funded this new computing platform.
sections.visual_cue: Logo of the U.S. National Science Foundation.
